body:
`store.RUST_BRIEF` tells an agent Rust's coding rules but not how to name or find code, so the first dozen calls of a Rust run go to guessing names. Add a few lines to the Rust brief in `Store::session` and `Store::task_session`, filled from the project's own store so the examples are real:

1. One method as `<module>.<Type>::<fn>` (a real one from the store), with "the module is the one holding the `impl`".
2. One test in an inline `mod tests`, as `<module>::tests.<name>`, and the `*** Add:` header that adds a test beside it.
3. "`find <text>` searches Rust source; `grep` searches other files only."
4. When the project has no method or no inline test module, leave that line out rather than inventing one.
5. Keep it to these lines; the full list is in the reference (task:5bc1e9311b667f05).
6. Tests: a Rust project's session shows a real method name and test name from its store; a project with no inline tests omits that line; a Gleam project's session is unchanged.

Checks: `rust-unit`, `rust-acceptance`.

Left out: examples chosen per task (e.g. from the task's named symbols).
title: session: Rust name examples from the project
